Current advances in the synthesis of beta-cyclodextrin-based metal organic frameworks and their potential applications in the adsorption/removal of pollutants: A comprehensive review

Parisa Ahmadi [a](#_bookmark0),[b](#_bookmark1), Azam Ahmadi [b](#_bookmark1), Mahnaz Tabibiazar [a](#_bookmark0),[\*](#_bookmark4), Samin Hamidi [c](#_bookmark2), Soghra Ramezani [d](#_bookmark3)

_Keywords:_

Metal organic framework Functionalization Modification

A B S T R A C T

Beta-cyclodextrin-based metal-organic frameworks (βCD-MOFs) are porous coordination compounds that represent a versatile class of renewable, biocompatible, edible, and non-toxic MOFs. These structures can be produced on a large scale by linking organic bridging ligands and metal ions. βCD-MOFs have increasingly attracted attention from researchers in the environmental sciences and food industry because of their high porosity, high specific surface area, tunability, and excellent biocompatibility features. This review focuses on the latest advances concerning these materials. First, a brief overview of the available technologies for the synthesis methods and structural properties of βCD-MOFs is introduced. Furthermore, the potential application of βCD-MOFs is highlighted by emphasizing the mechanisms of adsorption and removal of specific pollutants, such as dyes, heavy metals, nitroaromatics compounds, pesticides, and various volatile organic pollutants. Moreover, Challenges and future perspectives for practical applications of βCD-MOF were discussed.

# Introduction

In recent decades, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), a new class of hybrid crystalline micro or mesoporous coordination polymers, have attracted the attention of many researchers ([Xu et al., 2023](#_bookmark143)). Structur-ally, MOFs are constructed through self-assembled coordinate bonding between secondary building units, namely inorganic metal ion clusters (joints) and organic ligands (linkers) ([Nong et al., 2020](#_bookmark96)). These units are interconnected to form 3D lattices. MOFs evolved from polyhedral or small cluster coordination polymers, which were subsequently extended into one-dimensional chains, two-dimensional layers, and finally three-dimensional frameworks ([Kobielska et al., 2018](#_bookmark68)). The metal ions utilized in the synthesis of MOFs include alkali metals, transition metals, lan-thanides, alkaline earth metals, actinides, and p-block elements of the periodic table. Similarly, the organic linkers are sufficiently diverse to include phosphonate, carboxylate, imidazolate, sulfonate, pyridyl, azo-late functional groups, and aromatic or aliphatic linkers ([Rajkumar](#_bookmark104) [et al., 2019](#_bookmark104)).

Due to their considerable characteristics such as good thermal

stability, large specific surface area, abundant binding sites (open metal sites and ligands) for guest molecules, and variable pore sizes with tunable porosity, highly versatile MOFs have been applied extensively in various fields. These applications include gas storage and separations ([Hamedi et al., 2021](#_bookmark44); [Li et al., 2020](#_bookmark74)), adsorption ([Liu et al., 2019a](#_bookmark80); [Liu,](#_bookmark82) [Li, et al., 2017](#_bookmark82)), ion exchange ([Patel et al., 2017](#_bookmark98)), sensing ([Chang et al.,](#_bookmark28) [2022](#_bookmark28); [Zhang, Qi, Zhang, et al., 2023](#_bookmark152)), bio-imaging ([Chen, Ye, et al.,](#_bookmark29) [2017](#_bookmark29); [Chen, Zhang, et al., 2017](#_bookmark30)), drug delivery ([Chen et al., 2023](#_bookmark31); [Nie](#_bookmark93) [et al., 2023](#_bookmark93); [Rajamohan, Ashokkumar, et al., 2023](#_bookmark102)), electrocatalysis ([Zhao et al., 2022](#_bookmark156)), and photovoltaics ([Spoerke et al., 2017](#_bookmark118)).

Nonetheless, most MOFs are self-assembled using non-biodegradable and toxic metal nodes (e.g., Co, Cr, Ni, Gd) and non-food-grade organic linkers, which limit their use in various applications due to biocom-patibility, cytotoxicity, and environmental concerns ([Kathuria et al.,](#_bookmark66) [2023](#_bookmark66); [Lv et al., 2017](#_bookmark87)). Using biocompatible metal ions like Na, K, Cs, Ca, Fe, Zn, and Ti in the edible MOF synthesis as green approaches can help mitigate these concerns associated with some traditional MOFs that contain toxic metals. Furthermore, biologically acceptable linkers such as adenine nucleobase, porphyrins, peptides, carbohydrates (such as

cyclodextrins and carboxylic acids), amino acids or proteins, and oxa-lates have been used to synthesis of biocompatible MOFs ([He, Hou, et al.,](#_bookmark47) [2019](#_bookmark47); [Rajkumar et al., 2019](#_bookmark104); [Yang et al., 2019](#_bookmark145)). For example, the first peptide-based MOF fabricated using oligo-valine peptides as organic linkers to form bonds with Ca+2 centers was reported by Mantion et al.

([Mantion et al., 2008](#_bookmark88)).

In this regard, in recent years, naturally abundant cyclodextrins (CDs) have emerged as fascinating structural units for CD-based MOFs (CD-MOFs) synthesis. Due to the bidentate -OCCO- motifs on the pri-mary and secondary faces of CD molecules as shown in [Fig. 1](#_bookmark5) CD can coordinate with Group IA and IIA metal ions, especially sodium (Na+) or

potassium (K+) ions, to form extended structures of MOFs ([Forgan et al.,](#_bookmark41)

[2012](#_bookmark41)).

β-Cyclodextrin (βCD) is a kind of CD with high availability, low cost, intermediate size, and favorable formation of intermolecular hydrogen bonds, stable crystalline structure, and complex-forming capacities to-wards a wide range of substances. In terms of raw material costs, βCD is easily separated and purified, and its price is approximately one-thirtieth that of γCD. Consequently, βCD-MOFs offer the advantage of low production cost and significant potential for the industrial appli-cations ([Tian et al., 2021](#_bookmark125); [Zhao et al., 2023](#_bookmark157)).

Therefore, CD-MOFs are appropriate for different applications in drug delivery, gas adsorption, pollutant adsorption and removal, food packaging, encapsulation, catalyst, sensors, and etc. In this account, the aim of this review article was to provide a summary of (i) molecular structure and properties of βCD (ii) synthesis methodologies,

functionalization and modification attributes of βCD-MOFs, (iii) a gen-eral overview of their state-of-the-art applications as adsorbents.

# Overview of molecular structure and properties of βCD

- 1.  _A history of CDs discovery_

CDs were discovered from the enzymatic degradation by _Bacillus amylobactor_ grown on potato starch by French chemist Antoine Villiers in the late 19th century ([Villiers, 1891](#_bookmark128)). The main product of this fermentation was dextrin. The term dextrins was already used to describe starch degradation products. Villiers proposed naming this crystalline substance “cellulosine” due to its similarities with cellulose ([Crini, 2014](#_bookmark33)). A few years later (in 1891), the “Founding Father” of CD chemistry, Japanese scientist Franz Schardinger, identified two β-dextrin crystalline chemical compounds (crystalline dextrin A and crystalline dextrin B) from the fermentation products of potato starch-containing medium from newly isolated bacteria (_Bacillus macerans_). These substances were referred to as βCD or cyclomaltodextrin ([Szejtli,](#_bookmark123) [2004](#_bookmark123)).

- 1.  _CDs' molecular structure_

Generally, CDs are cyclic oligosaccharides that are frequently used to build supramolecular systems owing to their intrinsic uniform cavity and presence of abundance of –OH groups. The α-D-glucopyranose

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Fig. 1.** D-glucopyranoside structure (a), alpha, beta, and gamma-cyclodextrin structures (b), synthesis methods of Beta-cyclodextrin-based metal organic frame-works (c).

(glucose) units are linked together at carbons C1 and C4 via an α(1–4)-glycosidic bond. The most common structures known, as alpha (α), beta (β), and gamma (γ)-cyclodextrin, are made of 6, 7, and 8 units, respec-tively ([Dummert et al., 2022](#_bookmark36)). Based on the search results, the versatile adsorption properties, adaptability through modification, and environ-mentally friendly characteristics of βCD have made it as a strong candidate for environmental research for the adsorption of various pollutants ([Kamaraj et al., 2024](#_bookmark64)). Several reasons for this choice have been reported, mainly related to the limited adsorption capacity of αCD due to the smaller cavity size, as well as the hydrophobic nature of γCD, which leads to less solubility in aqueous environments. This can limit its effectiveness in water treatment applications, where high solubility is necessary for interaction with water-soluble pollutants ([Sikder et al.,](#_bookmark116) [2019](#_bookmark116)).

βCD is a non-reducing cyclic oligosaccharide containing of seven D-glucopyranoside units joined as α-(1 → 4) isomers. Its hollow, truncated ring is an amphiphilic toroidal or cone-shaped cylinder, with a pre-dominantly lipophilic central cavity and hydrophilic outer surface (formed by the hydroxyl (–OH) groups) ([Matencio et al., 2020](#_bookmark89)). Based on βCD architecture, the primary –OH groups are on the narrow side of the conical shape, while the secondary –OH groups are located on the wider edge of the toroidal shape ([Fig. 1](#_bookmark5)) ([Barman et al., 2018](#_bookmark22)). The hydrophobic cavity is where various guest molecules with suitable size and polarity can form inclusion complexes ([Oo et al., 2022](#_bookmark97)).

The hydrophobic tendency of the cavities in α, β, and γCD is a crucial

factor influencing their ability to form inclusion complexes with hy-drophobic molecules. The interior of these CDs is lined with ether-like oxygen atoms, while the exterior is decorated with hydroxyl (-OH) groups, which contribute to their hydrophilic nature ([Araújo et al.,](#_bookmark20) [2021](#_bookmark20)). For example, the βCD cavity is predominantly hydrophobic due to its ability to exclude water and other polar substances while still being

various guest molecules. The stability of these complexes is influenced by hydrogen bonding and van der Waals interactions, which are critical for practical applications ([Boroushaki & Dekamin, 2023](#_bookmark27)).

_2.4. Safety aspects_

Since 1998, the native βCD has been approved in the USA's Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) list, serving as a protectant and flavor carrier in various food products, at the concentration of 2 % ([Szente & Szejtli,](#_bookmark124) [2004](#_bookmark124)). The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) Panel on Food Ad-ditives and Nutrient Sources added to Food (ANS) has re-evaluated the safety of βCD (E 459) as a food additive. In 1996, the Scientific Com-mittee on Food (SCF) established an acceptable daily intake (ADI) of 5 mg/kg body weight per day to βCD ([Additives et al., 2016](#_bookmark16)) which in-dicates that βCD can be safely consumed at this level over a lifetime without significant risk. Some physicochemical properties of βCD are summarized in [Table 1](#_bookmark6).

Because of the large size and hydrophilic nature of βCD, it is poorly absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract following oral administration in humans and animals. Only small amounts are absorbed and rapidly excreted unchanged in urine, making it a safe option for use in various applications ([Stella & He, 2008](#_bookmark119)). Moreover, βCD exhibits low acute oral toxicity ([Additives et al., 2016](#_bookmark16)). Modified βCD derivatives like hydrox-ypropyl-βCD have improved safety profiles compared to the parent

its cavity; however, this inclusion does not significantly alter its hy-drophobic character ([Pereva et al., 2019](#_bookmark99)). The interactions between water molecules and the CD walls contribute to this stability, but the overall environment remains favorable for hydrophobic guest mole-cules. Inside the cavity, water molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other and with the CD walls, which stabilizes their arrangement without compromising the overall hydrophobic character. Moreover, the process of including guest molecules into CD cavities is energetically favorable due to the release of structured water molecules when a hydrophobic guest is introduced. This phenomenon enhances the driving force for complexation ([Jana & Bandyopadhyay, 2011](#_bookmark54)).

- 1.  _Solubility and thermodynamic stability_

CDs offer numerous advantages, including being water-soluble, tasteless, odorless, colorless, non-toxic, non-carcinogenic, non-caloric, economical, biodegradable, and biocompatible ([Xu et al., 2023](#_bookmark143)). βCD presents the least aqueous solubility (1.85 mg/mL, 4.5 mg/mL, and 9.1

mg/mL at 25 ◦C, 45 ◦C, and 60 ◦C, respectively) among three types of

CDs, is attributed to the formation of an intramolecular hydrogen bond belt between the –OH groups of the C2 carbons and –OH groups of C3 carbons ([Jansook et al., 2018](#_bookmark55)). These interactions make the structure rigid and prevent additional hydration by water molecules ([Miranda](#_bookmark91) [et al., 2011](#_bookmark91)). Furthermore, at high pH, ionization of hydroxyl groups increases water solubility; at pH 12.5 the solubility of βCD is 750 g/L ([Hedges, 2009](#_bookmark49)). In the case of αCD, the distorted position of one of the glycol-pyranose units allows for the formation of only four intra-molecular hydrogen bonds instead of six, as seen in γCD. This result leads to an incomplete hydrogen bond belt and thus better solubility in water. Likewise, the flexible nature of γCD molecules also enhances their water solubility ([Dummert et al., 2022](#_bookmark36)). Meanwhile, βCD has been frequently used pharmaceutical coating agent and targeted delivery. Studies have shown that βCD can form stable inclusion complexes with

They are less likely to cause kidney toxicity and hemolysis ([Loftsson & Brewster, 2010](#_bookmark84)). βCD does not readily decompose in the human stomach; whereas, it can be biodegraded in the gut by intestinal microbes and digestive enzymes, contributing to human metabolism as a common carbohydrate without any accumulation effects ([Fenyvesi](#_bookmark40) [et al., 2016](#_bookmark40)); consequently, βCD levels remain low (< 1 %) in tissues and

serum. Generally, the hydrolysis rate for the different types of CDs is as

follows: βCD ˂ αCD ˂ γCD ([Wei et al., 2023](#_bookmark138)).

# βCD-MOFs synthesis methods

For the βCD-MOFs synthesis, each βCD is self-assembly coordinated with four surrounding metal ions, while each metal ion links to seven oxygen atoms from four βCD units ([Li et al., 2021](#_bookmark76)).

CD-MOFs were commonly constructed using a solvent diffusion technique that requires small amounts of reactants. Other techniques such as hydro/solvothermal and ultrasound-assisted methods have also been employed. In this section, the details of different synthesis methods of βCD-MOFs are described ([Table 2](#_bookmark7), [Figs. 1](#_bookmark5)c & [2](#_bookmark8)a). Various factors including temperatures, reaction times, reactant concentrations, molar ratios, and solvents all play a substantial role in achieving good crys-tallinity and modulating crystal sizes ([Roy & Stoddart, 2021](#_bookmark107)).

- 1.  _Vapor diffusion method_

The vapor diffusion method is the most frequently used technique for preparing and developing βCD-MOFs. In this technique, an aqueous filtered solution of βCD and a metal salt in an appropriate stoichiometric ratio (typically 1:8) is placed in a glass container and allowed to stand for several days under solvent diffusion (methanol or ethanol) into the vapor chamber ([Dummert et al., 2022](#_bookmark36)). In essence, this method involves liquid–liquid diffusion, where the βCD-containing solution forms two phases based on their densities, the one phase is the precipitant βCD-MOF crystals, and the later phase contains the un-reacted βCD ([Xu et al.,](#_bookmark143) [2023](#_bookmark143)). Crystal growth also takes place as the precipitant solvent grad-ually diffuses into the separate layer, or when reactants in two vials with different sizes diffused through physical barriers. Following the vapor diffusion, the concentration of the reactants alters, leading to supersat-uration and subsequent nucleation and growth of βCD-MOF crystals ([Al](#_bookmark18) [Sharabati et al., 2022](#_bookmark18)). The collected βCD-MOFs crystals were washed with a suitable solvent (ethanol or methanol) several times to remove impurities and soaked in dichloromethane for 2–3 days, followed by

drying under vacuum at 40–50 ◦C for 24 h ([Hu et al., 2021](#_bookmark51)). Sadeh et al.

have also investigated the effect of several synthesis variables on the shape and size of βCD-MOF, focusing on obtaining a reduced size and uniform morphology for drug delivery applications. They examined various solvents (ethanol, methanol, acetonitrile, and acetone), reaction

times (6, 12, and 24 h), temperatures (40, 50, and 60 ◦C), βCD to KOH

molar ratios (1:4, 1:8, and 1:16), and amounts of cetyltrimethyl ammonium bromide (CTAB) (0, 56 and 112 mg). The optimal conditions identified were methanol as the solvent, 24 h reaction time, 60 ◦C re-

action temperature, molar ratio of βCD to KOH 1:8, and 112 mg CTAB surfactant, resulting in βCD-MOF with a mesoporous structure with 2.2 nm mean pore diameter and the size of 301 ± 13 nm ([Sadeh et al.,](#_bookmark108) [2023](#_bookmark108)). Although the vapor diffusion method is a reliable and repro-ducible classical method for preparing CD-MOFs, with the advantages of

obtaining high-quality crystalline materials and easily controlled crys-tallization reaction, its limitation is relatively low production efficiency and being a time-consuming process which can be overcome by using a low-boiling solvent ([Zhao et al., 2023](#_bookmark157)).

- 1.  _Hydro/solvothermal method_

The hydrothermal or solvothermal technique is a procedure con-ducted in pressure-resistant sealed vessels (reactors or autoclaves), under high ambient pressure, typically >1 atm, and a specific

temperature ranging from 100 ◦C to 200 ◦C, in the presence of water (hydrothermal) or organic solvents (solvothermal) ([Xu et al., 2023](#_bookmark143)). Generally, the nucleation and development of MOFs was influenced by

several parameters, including pressure, temperature, reaction time, reactant concentration and stoichiometry, type of solvent, additives or modifiers, and pH ([Lopez & Perez, 2023](#_bookmark85); [Qiu et al., 2020](#_bookmark101)). For the first time, Sha et al. synthesized βCD-MOFs with an “8”-type dual channel configuration and bowl-shaped pores through the solvothermal method

utilizing βCD and alkali metal (Na+/K+) ([Sha et al., 2015](#_bookmark110)). Additionally,

Lu et al. published the first demonstration of the preparation of chiral helices made using βCD molecules and sodium oxalate (1:4 M ratio) in

10 mL methanol and water (8:2, v/v) to create a βCD-MOF in a Teflon-lined reactor at 160 ◦C for three day period ([Lu et al., 2015](#_bookmark86)). The same procedure was applied to produce βCD-MOFs for detection of voltaic

organic compounds i.e., nitrobenzene and benzene ([Nikhar et al., 2021](#_bookmark94)). This method often results in a high yield of βCD-MOFs due to the favorable reaction conditions that promote crystallization. The ability to control temperature and pressure in a sealed environment enhances the solubility of reactants, facilitating more efficient formation of the desired framework (Haiyan [Li et al., 2017](#_bookmark73)). Besides these advantages, its drawbacks include energy consumption, time requirements (typically 24–72 h or more), formation of unwanted byproducts or trapped im-purities within the MOF structure, limited control over crystal morphology, and safety risks related to high-pressure conditions ([Xu](#_bookmark143) [et al., 2023](#_bookmark143)).

- 1.  _Ultrasound-assisted methods_

An ultrasound-assisted method has also been applied for the pro-duction of βCD-MOFs. This technique presents multiple advantages: they are simple, has rapid nucleation times, conserves energy, are environmentally friendly with high efficiency and yields, and can be carried out at room temperature ([Shen et al., 2022](#_bookmark115)). Furthermore, the cyclodextrin-based MOFs synthesized using ultrasound-assisted method were uniformly cubic in shape and measured approximately 8 μm in size ([Xu et al., 2023](#_bookmark143)).

The first study of CD-MOF synthesis by means of ultrasound was carried out by Hajra et al. in 2021. In their method, homogeneous aqueous solutions of cyclodextrin (α, β, and γ) and sodium bicarbonate were prepared by sonication for 10 min before adding trimesic acid. After 24 h, the solution was treated for another ten min of ultrasonic, and dimethylformamide was used to wash the crystals. They discovered that the βCD-MOF exhibited greater stability compared to the α and γCD-

MOFs, and all partially hydrated CD-MOFs remained stable up to 200 ◦C

under oxidative circumstances ([Hajra et al., 2021](#_bookmark42)). Due to the long duration and challenges associated with large-scale industrial produc-tion using the vapor diffusion method, L. Xu et al. developed amino-functionalized βCD-MOF by the ultrasonic technique, which shortened the fabrication process to approximately 2 h. The acoustic cavitation generated during ultrasonication resulted in a high temperature, increased the cooling rate, and consequently accelerated the synthesis process of NH2\-βCD-MOF ([Xu et al., 2019](#_bookmark142)). Ultrasound-assisted methods for synthesizing βCD-MOF offer significant advantages, including enhanced reaction rates and improved yield. However, challenges such as equipment costs, scalability, and potential degradation of materials must be carefully considered. Moreover, the heat produced by the ul-trasonic process can sometimes make it challenging to control the temperature of synthesis ([Zhao et al., 2023](#_bookmark157)). Overall, this synthesis method holds promise for producing high-quality βCD-MOFs with tailored properties for various applications.

**Fig. 2.** Synthesis methods (a) and modification/functionalization of βCD-MOFs, created with [Biorender.com](http://Biorender.com/).

([Fig. 2](#_bookmark8)b): 1) enhancing stability against chemical, thermal, and moisture-related degradation, 2) tailoring pore size and shape for spe-cific guest molecules and introducing functional groups to improve af-finity for target compounds, 3) adding catalytic sites for specific reactions, 4) increasing surface area for better adsorption of gases or pollutants or modifying surface chemistry to improve affinity for specific adsorbates, 5) creating stimuli-responsive behaviors (e.g. to pH, tem-perature, light), 6) enabling controlled release or capture of guest mol-ecules, 7) improving compatibility for biological applications, 8) reducing toxicity for potential medical uses, 9) introducing luminescent or photochromic properties and enabling sensing applications, 10) enhancing electrical or ionic conductivity for energy applications, 11) combining multiple functionalities in a single framework.

- 1.  _Modification/functionalization of βCD-MOF during the synthesis process_

Size control of βCD-MOF crystals is a crucial factor during the syn-thesis of CD-MOFs. The selection of appropriate additives such as CTAB and polyethylene glycol (PEG) significantly influences the properties and applications of βCD-MOF crystals. For example, CTAB coats the surface of forming MOF crystals, slowing their growth rate, which re-sults in smaller and more uniform crystals. Smaller crystal sizes can enhance the surface area available for interactions, making them more effective in the catalysis and drug delivery applications ([Han et al.,](#_bookmark45) [2020](#_bookmark45); [Lopez & Perez, 2023](#_bookmark85)). Moreover, CTAB can improve the stability of MOFs in aqueous environments by modifying their surface properties, where solubility is a key factor ([Lopez & Perez, 2023](#_bookmark85)). CTAB's ability to influence crystal morphology can lead to variations in pore size and distribution, which are critical for applications that depend on specific adsorption characteristics, such as gas storage or separation processes ([Sadeh et al., 2023](#_bookmark108)).

PEG can be considered as one of the best additives due to its low

toxicity and high ability to control the average diameter of the synthe-sized CD-MOF crystals ([Qiu et al., 2020](#_bookmark101)). The concentration of PEG inversely affects the size of the crystals; higher concentrations lead to smaller crystals. This size reduction can improve the loading capacity and release kinetics in delivery systems, making PEG-modified CD-MOFs suitable for biomedical applications ([Ahmadi et al., 2021](#_bookmark17)). Both CTAB and PEG allow for synthetic modifications that can tailor the CD-MOFs' properties. For example, PEG can be used to modify the surface chem-istry, affecting how the MOFs interact with other molecules, thus opti-mizing them for specific applications like targeted drug delivery or

imaging ([Ahmadi et al., 2021](#_bookmark17); [Qiu et al., 2020](#_bookmark101)).

In A. Yang et al. study, to synthesize the monodispersed βCD-MOFs crystals, following the solution recovery and transfer into another glass vial, 5 mL CTAB (8 mg/mL) was rapidly added. This can trigger fast precipitation of K-βCD-MOFs, reduce the crystallization time, and con-trol the growth of CD-MOF crystals ([Yang et al., 2019](#_bookmark145)). CTAB is a cationic surfactant utilized as a capping agent to control of the morphology and size of MOF crystals in aqueous systems ([Liu et al.,](#_bookmark79) [2016](#_bookmark79)). CTAB covers the surface of CD-MOF crystals in the crystallization medium, thereby slowing down the rate of crystals' growth and reducing their final size ([Qiu et al., 2020](#_bookmark101)). Additionally, the effect of different amounts of CTAB (0, 56, and 112 mg) on the vapor diffusion method for the βCD-MOFs synthesis was investigated. According to the SEM results, a reduction in the particle size was seen when the amount of CTAB increased. The long hydrocarbon chains of CTAB inhibit further growth of the structure. As the concentration increases, it caps the particles, declining the surface energy and preventing additional interaction with other particles and the next agglomerations ([Sadeh et al., 2023](#_bookmark108)). In W. Jiang et al. study, two types of metal organic frameworks (K-βCD-MOFs and Cs-βCD-MOFs) were produced through a modified solvent diffusion method which toxic CTAB was replaced by green PEG20000, as an efficient size modulator ([Jiang et al., 2021](#_bookmark62)). In the Yubin Zhang et al. study, citric acid (CA) modified βCD (CA-βCD) was first synthesized by chemical grafting, followed by the synthesis of the final product, CA-βCD-MOF, using a vapor diffusion method. While βCD-MOF completely dissolves in water, CA-βCD-MOF demonstrates greater water stability than βCD-MOF, which increases with higher concentrations of CA.

Moreover, the adsorption effectiveness of Congo Red (CR) dye and

copper ions (Cu2+) were improved for CA-βCD-MOF compared to βCD-MOF. This enhancement can be attributed to introducing of -COOH

groups and the availability of more new adsorption sites after the CD modification with CA ([Zhang, Zhang, Wang, et al., 2023](#_bookmark155)).

- 1.  _Post-Modifications/fictionization of βCD-MOF_

Carboxylation of one –OH group of βCD enhanced the stability of βCD-MOF in water and increased the number of adsorption sites, facil-itating complexation-based adsorption of some pollutants. Additionally, CA is an environmentally friendly, small-molecule crosslinker that can fully interact with cyclodextrin, effectively improving the efficiency of modification ([Ding et al., 2021](#_bookmark35)). In this regard, the synthesis of an eco-friendly CA-βCD-MOF was accomplished in two steps: preparing pri-mary βCD-MOF through a hydrothermal process and modifying it with

CA (cl-CD@CA). The modified cl-CD@CA nanocubes exhibited a considerable reduction in size after the crosslinking reaction, likely because of the breaking of coordination bonds within the crystals of βCD-MOF. This indicates that the thermal crosslinking reaction happens randomly throughout the βCD-MOF, contributing to the formation of the crosslinked moieties (cl-CD@CA), while the uncross-linked βCD-MOF dissolves and is removed during washing. Increasing the amount of CA led to the filling of more pores in βCD-MOF, which in turn led to lower specific surface areas for cl-CD@CA samples compared to the βCD-MOF. Simultaneously, the crosslinking between βCD and CA may have trans-formed the small pores of βCD-MOF (4.66 nm) into larger pores (over 15 nm). The solubility of cl-CD@CA dramatically decreased to 0.5 mg/mL, in contrast to the high solubility of βCD and βCD-MOF at room tem-perature (18.3 and 19.7 mg/mL, respectively). This reduction can be related to CA molecules tightly binding the -OH groups in βCD, pre-venting the MOF structure from collapsing. Ultimately, these MOFs demonstrated multiple adsorption sites and high water stability through modification with CA ([Jia et al., 2023](#_bookmark56)).

In a recent study, a novel modified βCD-MOF was synthesized by

inducing the crystallization of βCD and potassium chloride (KCl), fol-lowed by thermal cross-linking with pre-added CA in CD-MOF and subsequent grafting with chitosan (CS). The CD-MOF/CA yield was measured as 64.5 %. The crystals of the CD-MOF/CA were transformed into the nanocubes of CD/CA-_g_\-CS during crosslinking and grafting processes, significantly reducing in their size to 171.7 nm. The larger CDMOF/CA crystals, owing to its loose and porous nature, were more susceptible to broken down and formation of the nano-sized CD/CA-g-CS cubes during the heating and grafting. Moreover, the CD/CA-g-CS exhibited exceptional water stability after 1 h of ultrasonication since the its mass loss in water was only 0.3 g/L, considerably lower than CD-MOF/CA (26.5 g/L) and βCD (18.5 g/L). Consequently, highly water-stable CD/CA-g-CS can be a promising material for industrial waste-water treatment applications ([Jia, Wu, et al., 2024](#_bookmark57)).

In X. Sun et al. study, the carboxymethylated βCD-MOF was grafted

onto the surface of titanium dioxide (TiO2) by covalent bonding. They used cyanamide as an activator to form the CD-MOF/TiO2 adsorbent which can exist stably in an aqueous environment. The final composite inherits the CDs' adsorption properties, the MOFs' high specific surface area, and titanium dioxide water stability. This unique integration re-sults in high selective adsorption capacities of organochlorine pesticides from water ([Sun et al., 2022](#_bookmark121)).

In the most recent study, the aminopyrimidine-modified βCD-MOF (AP-βCD-MOF) with glutaraldehyde as a cross-linking agent was syn-thesized at room temperature. This process introduces additional adsorption sites and enhances the thermal and water stability of βCD-MOF. Additionally, the amount of amino pyrimidine grafted onto βCD-MOF can affect how effectively the pollutants adsorb, which AP-βCD-MOF with 1:1 mass ratios showed the best adsorption efficiency ([Zhang](#_bookmark154) [et al., 2024](#_bookmark154)).

Furthermore, facile yet efficient βCD-MOF-based porous hydrogels were formed by incorporating a crosslinked hydrogel network based on

_N_, _N_′-methylenebis(acrylamide) (MBA) and acrylic acid (AA) monomers

in βCD-MOF under ultrasonication. After adding MeOH to the mixture as

a crystal induce, the synthesized MOFs were collected, thoroughly washed with MeOH, and dried under a vacuum for 24 h. The synthesized A/M- CDMOF-porous hydrogel demonstrated improved structural sta-bility and excellent properties for simultaneous adsorption of heavy metals ([Jia, Zhu, et al., 2024](#_bookmark58)). C. Liu, Wang, Liu, Yi, Zhou, et al. employed a thermal decomposition of βCD-MOF in the synthesis of multifunctional MOF-derived nanoporous carbon (βCD-MOF-NPC), consisting of βCD and potassium benzoate. Thermogravimetric analysis

indicated that βCD-MOF-NPC had good thermal stability up to 600 ◦C.

During the high-temperature carbonization process, βCD underwent decomposition, while the resulting pyrolytic carbon material still possessed numerous functional groups that could provide the affinity for binding between βCD-MOF-NPC and organic pollutants ([Liu et al.,](#_bookmark81)

[2019b](#_bookmark81)).

A modified vapor diffusion method incorporating CTAB was accomplished for the synthesis of biocompatible K-βCD-MOFs enabling curcumin delivery to cancerous cells. L-glutamine-functionalized βCD-MOF (glutamine-βCD-MOF) improved the specificity of the MOFs for cancer cell targeting, because of glutamine's indispensable role in the proliferation of cancer cells and energy metabolism. Additionally, the introduction of amino group provided further opportunities for func-tionalization. Consequently, coating the MOFs with gelatin (gelat-in@βCD-MOF) facilitated controlled drug release in an acidic medium ([Sadeh et al., 2024](#_bookmark109)).

- 1.  _Electrospun βCD-MOFs_

Electrospun fibers of biosafe βCD-MOF/polycaprolactone (βCD-MOF/PCL) were synthesized through a CD precursor doping method, followed by hydrothermal vapor diffusion treatment. To create the βCD-MOF precursor solution, βCD and K2CO3 (as the potassium source K+) at

0.5:4 mmol ratio were dissolved in water at 60 ◦C. The already syn-

thesized PCL/βCD fibers were suspended vertically in the βCD-MOF precursor solution in a vial, allowing methanol vapor diffusion in a sealed large jar. The samples reacted in a water bath at 50 ◦C for 24 h.

After the reaction, the samples were cooled for 30 min, removed, washed with absolute ethanol, and dried to obtain CD-MOF/PCL fibrous membranes ([Wang, Huang, et al., 2023](#_bookmark131)).

# βCD-MOFs characterization techniques

Multiple characterization methods and instruments can be applied to investigate the CD-MOFs properties.

- 1.  _Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) analysis_

FTIR spectra are performed on βCD and βCD-MOF to explore their chemical structure and functional groups involved in the reaction ([Fig. 3](#_bookmark9)a). The spectrum of the βCD shows a broad peak between 3400 and 3200 cm—1, associated with symmetric stretching of O–H groups in the βCD cyclic structure, which is necessary for hydrophilicity ([Jia et al.,](#_bookmark56)

[2023](#_bookmark56)). Notably, this peak can be also seen in the βCD-MOF spectrum with a slight shifted position to around 3381 cm—1, indicating that the –OH groups remain intact after coordination. A sharp absorption band is observed around 2923 cm—1, within the range of 3000–2850 cm—1, corresponding to the asymmetric stretching of CH2 band. Additionally, a peak at 1649 cm—1 represents the bending vibrations of O–H group due to the presence of water molecules in the βCD cavity. The existence of peaks at 1418 cm—1 and 1337 cm—1 are due to deformation vibrations of the C–H bonds in the primary and secondary hydroxyl groups of βCD

([Shahzaib, Ahmad, et al., 2023](#_bookmark112)). Furthermore, the absorption peaks at 1029 cm—1 and 1158 cm—1 correspond to the C-O-C stretching vibration bonds in the pyranose ring and glycosidic linkage ([Dehghani et al.,](#_bookmark34) [2020](#_bookmark34)). These significant peaks can be observed in the FTIR spectrum of βCD-MOF, signifying the presence of βCD in the MOF. The shift in the

bands indicates the interaction between βCD and metal ions. Conse-quently, the parent βCD skeleton structure is maintained in βCD-MOFs, as demonstrated by the comparison of the FTIR spectra of βCD and βCD-MOFs ([Rajamohan, Raorane, et al., 2023](#_bookmark103)).

- 1.  _X-ray diffraction (XRD)_

XRD is a valuable technique to investigate the crystalline structure of CDs. CDs are crystalline materials characterized by either “cage” or “channel” type crystal structures. The pristine commercial βCD can aggregate into cage-like structures with “herring-bone” arrangements, where the cavity of each molecule is blocked by the adjacent molecule ([Uyar et al., 2009](#_bookmark127)). When βCD coordinates to metal nodes, this arrangement transitions to channel form. In the channel configuration,

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Fig. 3.** FTIR spectra (a) and XRD patterns (b) of βCD and βCD-MOFs.

the CD molecules are aligned and stacked on top of one another, forming long cylindrical channels. Typically, the presence of this channel structure in CDs serves as the coordination confirmation ([Sadeh et al.,](#_bookmark108) [2023](#_bookmark108)).

According to [Fig. 3](#_bookmark9)b, the XRD patterns of these two arrangements differ, indicating the formation of metal-organic frameworks. The nar-row peak shapes indicate that the materials possess relatively high

crystallinity ([Sadeh et al., 2024](#_bookmark109)). βCD showed some distinct peaks at 9.02◦, 10.78◦, 12.62◦, 15.38◦, 16.98◦, 18.88◦, 19.58◦, 22.66◦, 27.06◦,

31.86◦, 34.84◦, 39.64◦, and 51.30◦ ([Jiang, Liu, et al., 2022](#_bookmark59)). Compared to βCD, many peaks in the XRD patterns shifted slightly or disappeared, and some new sharp characteristic peaks appeared at 6.5◦, 12.14◦, 14.2◦, 18.06◦, 19.22◦, 24.40◦, 28.52◦, and 30.42◦. These changes indi-

cate the presence of new crystalline phases in βCD-MOFs. The changes

observed in the XRD patterns clearly demonstrate the interactions be-tween CDs and metal ions, resulting in formation of βCD-MOF ([Hu et al.,](#_bookmark51) [2021](#_bookmark51)).

- 1.  _Thermal stability_

The differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) are used to determine the thermodynamic properties of the MOFs. DSC is a method used to determine phase transition tem-peratures (Tm: melting temperature and Tg: glass transition tempera-ture) ([Leyva-Porras et al., 2019](#_bookmark72)). TGA is a technique applied to assess the thermal stability and degradation behavior of materials by measuring weight changes as a function of temperature ([Healy et al., 2020](#_bookmark48)).

DSC thermogram of βCD exhibits two heat absorption peaks: the first appears at ~100 ◦C which is related to the water evaporation from the crystals; the second, occurring at ~250 ◦C, is a result of crystal melting and thermal decomposition ([Hedges, 2009](#_bookmark49)).

Furthermore, multiple steps of weight loss are observed in the TGA thermograms for both βCD and βCD-MOF in the temperature range of 25 ◦C to 700 ◦C; the first weight loss occurs within the temperature range

of 40–100 ◦C, corresponding to the loss of water and/or the residual

solvent molecules ([Hu et al., 2022](#_bookmark52)); a significant weight loss in the second step occurs at >270 ◦C, predominantly related to the structural collapse owing to breakage of the crosslinking bonds and βCD decom-

position ([Shahzaib, Ahmad, et al., 2023](#_bookmark112); [Zhang et al., 2024](#_bookmark154)). The degradation temperature of βCD-MOF, estimated from the peak of the derivative TGA curves, is found to be approximately 300 ◦C. This in-dicates that the thermal decomposition process is started by the opening

of cyclodextrin rings, followed by a degradation pattern characterized

by the loss of the hydroxyl groups and glucosidic structures, resulting in the formation of the unsaturated moieties such as aromatic structures and carbonyl groups ([Hajra et al., 2021](#_bookmark42)). The remaining material that slowly decreased after this second drop was the inorganic metal, which needed higher temperatures to degrade completely ([Ez et al., 2023](#_bookmark38)).

Generally, βCD-MOFs may exhibit improved thermal stability compared to pure βCD due to the stabilizing effects of metal coordina-tion, but this can vary based on specific synthesis conditions and the nature of the metal used. For example, the degradation patterns of Cu-βCD-MOF and Ni- βCD-MOF illustrate a significant increase in thermal stability compared to pure βCD, which can be ascribed to the metal ions incorporation ([Shahzaib, Shaily, et al., 2023b](#_bookmark114)); whereas, Hu, Z., et al. study reported the decrease in thermal stability of MOFs that can be explained by the porous structures and weaker metal-coordination bonds ([Hu et al., 2021](#_bookmark51)). According to their results, the βCD-MOF ex-hibits significantly greater thermal stability than both αCD-MOF and γCD-MOF, indicating its stronger crystalline structure. Thermal stability is a crucial factor in development of CD-MOF materials, for application to heat-stabilization of organic compounds; therefore βCD-MOF has the potential aimed at thermostability improvement of compounds ([Hu](#_bookmark51) [et al., 2021](#_bookmark51)). Some details of DSC and TGA results of βCD and βCD-MOF are summarized in [Table 3](#_bookmark10).

- 1.  _Solubility_

Water solubility is crucial in assessing the recyclability of βCD-based adsorbents, evaluated through intuitive and quantitative methods. The solubility in water was determined by calculating the mass dissolved in 1 L of deionized water. Both βCD and βCD-MOFs dissolve rapidly into transparent aqueous solutions within 30 s of ultrasonic treatment, with reported solubilities at room temperature of 18.3 mg/mL and 19.7 mg/ mL, respectively ([Jia et al., 2023](#_bookmark56)). In another study, the corresponding solubility of βCD and βCD-MOFs was 18.6 mg/mL and 21.5 mg/mL, respectively ([Jia, Wu, et al., 2024](#_bookmark57)).

The water contact angle also provides quantitative data on the wettability of the solid surface, offering an approximate estimation of the hydrophobic or hydrophilic characteristics. For powder materials, the measured contact angle is typically smaller due to the roughness and porosity of the produced pellets ([Ke et al., 2019](#_bookmark67)). The favorable hy-drophilicity is ascribed to the presence of abundant –COOH and –OH groups on the surfaces of the adsorbents, allowing them to form complexation with contaminants in water rapidly ([Jia et al., 2023](#_bookmark56)).

- 1.  _BET_

Nitrogen adsorption-desorption measurement of MOFs can be uti-lized to assess their permanently porous nature through Bru-nauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis ([Zhang et al., 2020](#_bookmark150)). The pore volume distribution pore size, and specific surface area, of MOFs are crucial indicators for characterizing the physicochemical properties of mesoporous materials including their adsorption performance, catalytic activity, and separation efficiency. A larger specific surface area enabled a higher loading capacity ([Bai et al., 2024](#_bookmark21)). The details of surface areas (m2/g), pore diameters (nm or Å), and pore volume (cm3/g) are mentioned in [Table 2](#_bookmark7).

- 1.  _Structural diversity_

Structural diversity in CD-MOFs encompasses the diverse structural configurations and spatial arrangements arising from the strategic co-ordination of cyclodextrins with various metal ions. Characteristically, these materials exhibit a typical monoclinic structure. By taking advantage of the asymmetric –OCCO– bridging units, CD molecules facilitate coordinated bonding with group IA and IIA metal cations enabling the formation of extended 3D networks ([Li et al., 2023](#_bookmark75)).

The distinctive architecture of the K-CD-MOFs is characterized by a complex dual-pore structures comprising: bowl-like cavities and inter-connected 8-shaped dual channel arrangements. Specifically, two adja-cent βCDs are coordinated by a potassium ion through a unique “T”-shape arrangement, forming a distinctive bowl-like structure ([Yang](#_bookmark145) [et al., 2019](#_bookmark145)). In this configuration, one βCD unit contributes its 2- and 3-hydroxyl groups from _a_\- and _d_\-1,4-linked D-glucopyranosyl rings, while the complementary CD unit provides 6-hydroxyl and 2- and 3-hydroxyl

groups from _b_\- and _D_\-glucopyranosyl. Furthermore, the βCD molecules and K+ cations establish coordinated interactions that form a one-dimensional chain structure, with these “T” structural units aligned along the crystallographic a-axis to generate an “8”- type double channel network. Ultimately, each double channel unit is interconnected

through the K–O interactions along the a-axis, resulting in a compre-hensive 3D K-CD-MOFs structure ([Li et al., 2023](#_bookmark75)).

In contrast to the previously reported KOH-βCD-MOF, the βCD-POF (with KI) framework demonstrates a distinct structural transformation mechanism. Instead of generating novel cavities, the framework mod-ifies existing cavity configurations by interconnecting βCD molecules through K+ ion coordination, transforming their cavities into elongated,

parallel tubular structures ([Zhang, Chen, Zhang, et al., 2023](#_bookmark153)).

Several studies have revealed that βCD-MOF possesses unique structural characteristics that enable drug molecule encapsulation. These frameworks contain the bowl-like porous configurations and intricate channel structures that facilitate effective trapping of various compounds within their molecular cavities ([Sha et al., 2015](#_bookmark110)).

According to the SEM images, the Cu-βCD-MOF exhibits a rod-like morphological configuration ([Shahzaib, Ahmad, et al., 2023](#_bookmark112); [Tu et al.,](#_bookmark126) [2020](#_bookmark126)), which may be attributed to a complex interplay of critical syn-thesis parameters, including solvent composition (water/EtOH), the reaction conditions, and presence of copper metal ions.

The Cu-based MOFs morphology exhibits a pronounced temperature-dependent transformation. At low and moderate temperatures, rod-shaped crystals predominantly develop, while high temperatures typi-cally induce the formation of rounded crystal configurations ([Shahzaib,](#_bookmark112) [Ahmad, et al., 2023](#_bookmark112)). Furthermore, βCD-MOF exhibits a regular shape characterized by either cubic ([Zhang et al., 2024](#_bookmark154); [Zhang, Zhang, Wang,](#_bookmark155) [et al., 2023](#_bookmark155)) or rectangular geometric configurations ([Bai et al., 2024](#_bookmark21)).

# Application of βCD-MOFs as pollutants' adsorbent

With the continuous economy development and world population growth, various pollutants are produced due to human activities. These pollutants can be detected across various environmental media, posing serious threats to the ecological environment and human health ([Yang](#_bookmark146) [et al., 2023](#_bookmark146)). Recent studies have demonstrated that MOFs are capable of adsorbing and removing diverse rages of pollutants such as heavy metals, dyes, nitroaromatic compounds pesticides, volatile organic compounds, and antibiotics owing to their large specific surface areas, tunable pre size, and high adsorption capacities ([Jia, Wu, et al., 2024](#_bookmark57); [Liu et al., 2019b](#_bookmark81); [Wang et al., 2018](#_bookmark132)). An overview of the adsorption condition and efficiency of βCD-MOFs in the adsorption/removal of various pollutants is summarized in [Table 4](#_bookmark11). Furthermore, removal mechanisms and analysis techniques are shown in [Fig. 4](#_bookmark12).

- 1.  _Heavy metals_

Heavy metals (HMs) are metallic or metalloid elements character-ized by high atomic weight and a density that is at least five times greater than that of water ([Abd Elnabi et al., 2023](#_bookmark14)). HMs mainly origi-nate from industrial activities such as mining, electroplating, smelting, and tanning industries, with contamination being particularly severe in developing countries. Different heavy metals, including copper (Cu), cadmium (Cd), chromium (Cr), lead (Pb), nickel (Ni), mercury (Hg), zinc (Zn), and arsenic (As), are recognized as biologically unnecessary and detrimental to the aquatic ecosystem ([Abd Elnabi et al., 2023](#_bookmark14)). HMs can directly or indirectly pose significant risks to ecosystem sustainability and human health through drinking water, skin contact and the food chain due to their non-biodegradability, stability, bioaccumulation ca-pacity in organisms within the ecosystem, and high toxicity levels ([Chen](#_bookmark32) [et al., 2020](#_bookmark32); [Rostami et al., 2024](#_bookmark106)). Therefore, establishing effective methods to remove toxic heavy metal ions from the environment has become a crucial research aim. HMs adsorbent systems utilize various materials to capture and remove heavy metal ions effectively. The key

**Fig. 4.** Specific removal mechanisms and analysis techniques applied for different pollutants through βCD-MOF.

materials commonly employed in adsorption-based separation can be classified into several categories ([Qasem et al., 2021](#_bookmark100); [Zaimee et al.,](#_bookmark149) [2021](#_bookmark149)): 1) carbonaceous materials (such as activated carbon, carbon nanotubes, graphene, and graphene oxide), 2) chitosan-based adsor-bents, 3) inorganic adsorbents (nano alumina fibers, alumina and zeo-lites), 4) biosorbents, and 5) metal-organic frameworks adsorbents, and

6) biomass-derived materials (microalgae and agricultural waste). Due to their unique properties of MOFs, they have emerged as promising adsorbents for the removal of heavy metals.

Eco-friendly βCD-based nanocubes (βCD-MOF crosslinked with citric acid, cl-CD@CA) extraordinary adsorption capacity were fabricated using a facile and cost-effective technique to treat textile dyeing efflu-ents. The synthesized adsorbents demonstrated high water stability and remarkable capacity towards the adsorption of Pb2+, Cd2+, and Sb3+

ions, with corresponding maximum adsorption capacity of 758.7, 525.3,

and 398.1 mg/g. These cl-CD@CA MOFs preserved outstanding recy-clability after 10 regeneration cycles. Notably, cl-CD@CA displayed high dynamic and static adsorption capacities, achieving concentration reductions of 95 %, 29 %, and 16 % for Pb2+, Cd2+, and Sb3+, respec-tively ([Jia et al., 2023](#_bookmark56)). Yubin Zhang et al. developed a recyclable

adsorbent using CA-modified βCD MOFs for remove heavy metals. As a result, the maximum adsorption capacity for the copper ions (Cu2+) reached an impressive 287.4 mg/g. The Cu2+ adsorption was attributed to the complexation between Cu2+ and the carboxyl group on CA. Consequently, the CA-βCD-MOF demonstrated excellent recyclability

and adsorption performance, demonstrating considerable potential in heavy metals removal from aqueous solution ([Zhang, Zhang, Wang,](#_bookmark155) [et al., 2023](#_bookmark155)).

- 1.  _Dyes_

Dyes are substances that contain chromophores responsible for color, giving them coloring ability. They have been expansively utilized in textiles, printing, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, fiber products, plastics, and more ([Hosny et al., 2023](#_bookmark50)). Dyes can be classified based on their ionic charges (including basic, acidic, vat, direct, and biting dyes) or ac-cording to their chemical structure (anthraquinone, azo dyes, indigoid, phthalocyanines, xanthene, nitrates, and nitrous) ([Berradi et al., 2019](#_bookmark23)). However, dyes are poisonous chemicals which can pose substantial threats to the ecosystem. Additionally, their residues can enter the food chain and lead to food safety concerns and chronic diseases ([Yang et al.,](#_bookmark148) [2020](#_bookmark148)). Moreover, the dyes present in dyeing effluent are typically toxic, with some being synthetic and non-biodegradable, contributing to the chromaticity and eutrophication of water bodies, and causing further pollution of the aquatic environment ([Bilal et al., 2022](#_bookmark25)). Because of these problems, efficient removal technologies are required for envi-ronmental management.

The low-cost versatile nano-adsorbent βCD-MOF/CA has been syn-

thesized by chemically binding of βCD with CS and CA for highly effi-cient dyes scavenging. The βCD/CA_\-g-_CS exhibits extremely high adsorption capacities of 946.66, 801.66, and 770.50 mg/g for the cationic dyes of methylene blue (MB), malachite green (MG), and basic red (BR), respectively. It also demonstrates impressive capacities of 619.60, 429.22, and 389.64 mg/g for the anionic dyes acid red (AR), acid yellow (AY), and acid blue (AB), respectively ([Jia, Wu, et al., 2024](#_bookmark57)). Meanwhile, in another study, CA modified-CD-MOF (with a molar dosing ratio of 1:1 for βCD to CA) was identified as the optimum adsorbent for the anionic dye CR, exhibiting super adsorption capacity of 900.9 mg/g. The adsorption process was determined to be endo-thermic and spontaneous. The combination of the experimental results and density functional theory calculations confirmed that the primary adsorption mechanism for CR is electrostatic interaction ([Zhang, Zhang,](#_bookmark155) [Wang, et al., 2023](#_bookmark155)).

- 1.  _Nitroaromatic compounds_

Nitro-compounds represent an important category of pollutants and are valuable intermediate in various industrial applications. Nitro-compounds with an aromatic base are mainly used as starting mate-rials for commercial purposes, while their aliphatic variants illustrate a more diverse chemical behavior under reducing conditions ([Haleem](#_bookmark43) [et al., 2023](#_bookmark43)). Based on chemical structure, nitroaromatic compounds (NACs) can be mainly categorized into two groups: aliphatic (such as alkenes, alkanes, and alkyne compounds) and aromatic (such as het-erocyclic, cyclic, and planer) ([Kumar et al., 2020](#_bookmark71)).

NACs widely exist in the aquatic, atmospheric, terrestrial environ-ment, as well as in human foods. They are a type of aromatic compound characterized by the presence of at least one nitro group (-NO2) on the benzene ring ([Ju & Parales, 2010](#_bookmark63)). These compounds display unique electronegativity, electron affinity, and reduction potential. Another key feature of NACs is their capability to function as electron-donor mate-rials ([Bilal et al., 2021](#_bookmark24)). The nitro group located on the benzene ring has high electronegativity that causes delocalization of the ring's π-elec-trons, satisfying own charge deficiency. The primary reaction step used to synthesize nitroaromatic compounds is nitration. Nitronium ions

(NO+) are generated through sulfuric acid and nitric acid combination.

2

These ions can react with aromatic substrates in an electrophilic sub-stitution ([Ju & Parales, 2010](#_bookmark63)). This property of NACs along with stable benzene rings can make NACs as materials resistant to oxidative degradation ([Bilal et al., 2021](#_bookmark24)). NACs pose significant risks to human health and natural ecosystems owing to their high toxicity and carci-nogenic properties. The United States Environmental Protection Agency has classified these compounds as hazardous pollutants. Long-term exposure to NACS increases serious public health and food safety con-cerns ([EPA, 2013](#_bookmark37); [Kumar et al., 2020](#_bookmark71)). Consequently, it is essential to implement practical and efficient measures to minimize or eliminate their presence in the environment.

The preparation of βCD-MOF coordinated with nickel incorporation (Ni-βCD-MOF) for the catalytic reduction of NACs was achieved using a simple and sustainable vapor deposition technique. The Ni-βCD-MOF manifested impeccable performance in reducing nitroaromatics com-pounds (≤ 5 min). Therefore, Ni-βCD-MOF can be utilized as a catalyst

for eliminating the toxic compounds in water treatment ([Shahzaib,](#_bookmark113)

[Shaily, et al., 2023a](#_bookmark113)). In another study, the applicability of Cu-βCD-MOF was investigated in the catalytic reduction of NACs, namely 4- Nitro-aniline (4-NA), 4-Nitrophenol (4-NP), 2-Nitrophenol (2-NP), and Nitrobenzene (NB). Cu-βCD-MOF revealed high catalytic activity, effectively reducing all NACs in <4 min ([Shahzaib, Ahmad, et al., 2023](#_bookmark112)).

- 1.  _Pesticides_

In the agricultural and industrial sectors, the mass production and utilization of agrochemicals, especially pesticides, have resulted in surface and groundwater contamination. As living standards grow and the global population demands more food, the production and appli-cation of pesticides continue to increase ([Mondol & Jhung, 2021](#_bookmark92)). Pes-ticides are chemicals used to protect crops from pests and plant diseases while promoting agricultural growth ([Karimi-Maleh et al., 2024](#_bookmark65)). Pes-ticides are classified into four categories based on their use in agricul-ture: insecticides, herbicides, bactericides, and acaricides. The most common active ingredients in these pesticides include chlorinated hy-drocarbons, organophosphates, carbamates, and carbamide derivatives ([Huang et al., 2018](#_bookmark53)). According to the statistics from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) in 2022, total pesticides usage in the agriculture reached 3.70 million tonnes of active ingredients, representing a 4 % increase compared to 2021, a 13 % in-crease over the past decade, and a doubling since 1990 ([FAO, 2022](#_bookmark39)). The improper usage of pesticides and their residues pose substantial threats to the environment and multiple health hazards to humans, leading to various issues including bioaccumulation in the food chain, resistance to

pathogens and pests, loss of biodiversity, water erosion, and soil degradation ([Abdollahdokht et al., 2022](#_bookmark15); [Karimi-Maleh et al., 2024](#_bookmark65)). Consequently, the effective removal of pesticides from the food chains and aqueous environment has attracted researchers' attention.

In a study, multifunctional βCD-MOFs-derived porous carbon possessed efficient adsorptive removal performance of four amide her-bicides acetochlor (ACE), alachlor (ALA), metolachlor (MET), and pre-tilachlor (PRE), as typical pollutants in agricultural wastewater, which maximum adsorption capacities were in the range of 261.21–343.42 mg/g ([Liu et al., 2019b](#_bookmark81)). In another study, a hybrid nanocomposite was prepared by grafting βCD-MOF as an organic ligand onto titanium di-oxide. The material combines the CD's adsorption properties, the MOFs' high specific surface area structure, and the titanium dioxide stability in the water, which was used as a dispersive solid-phase extraction adsorbent to extract the organochlorine pesticides residues in the honey with recovery in the range of 76.4 to 114.3 % ([Sun et al., 2022](#_bookmark121)).

- 1.  _Volatile organic compounds_

Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are an important group of air pollutants generated by industrial activities, vehicle emissions, petro-chemical processing, solvent production, painting, commercial prod-ucts, and other sources of pollution ([He, Cheng, et al., 2019](#_bookmark46)). When these compounds are released into the atmosphere, they participate in the synthesis of photochemical smog, secondary organic aerosols, and ground ozone, which have detrimental effects on climate change, eco-systems, air quality, and human health, causing headaches, mutagen-esis, cancer, and teratogenesis, even at low concentrations ([Mellouki](#_bookmark90) [et al., 2015](#_bookmark90); [Siu et al., 2023](#_bookmark117)). VOCs are defined as organic substances with low water solubility and high vapor pressure ([Koppmann, 2020](#_bookmark70)). They can be categorized into various classes based on some factors such as boiling point, molecular structure, and polarity ([Zhu et al., 2020](#_bookmark159)). Therefore, because of the serious risks that VOCs pose to public health and the environment, extensive efforts are needed to develop effective strategies for removing these pollutants from the air while minimizing environmental impact.

The biosafe βCD-MOF/polycaprolactone (βCD-MOF/PCL) electro-

spun fiber membranes were synthesized by doping them with cyclo-dextrin precursor, followed by hydrothermal treating in a solvent vapor diffusion process to cause the CD-MOFs in-situ growth on the electro-spun fibers. The CD-MOF/PCL demonstrates significantly superior per-formance in VOCs (styrene, benzaldehyde, and aniline, as widely used organic compounds in industrial products) uptake compared to PCL-CD membrane and N95 mask filter cotton. While CDs possess a unique performance to encapsulation of molecules within their cavities to form inclusions, the PCL-CD sample exhibits weak VOC uptake. This limited ability may be attributed to the hydrophobic nature of the CD cavity. In contrast, the CD-MOF/PCL effectively removes VOCs, which can be credited to the presence of βCD-MOF ([Wang, Huang, et al., 2023](#_bookmark131)).

- 1.  _Antibiotics_

Antibiotics are organic compounds that effectively inhibit the harmful microorganisms growth and are widely utilized in human and animal medicine, as well as in aquaculture and agriculture ([Sun, Qiao,](#_bookmark122) [et al., 2023](#_bookmark122)). Nevertheless, the large-scale and unreasonable use of an-tibiotics raises significant global concerns, leading to challenges in their removal during treatment processes, allowing them to persist in the environment, and contributing to the spread of antibiotic-resistant bacteria ([Wei et al., 2021](#_bookmark139)). Furthermore, antibiotics can enter the human body through the food chain, disrupting normal metabolic pro-cesses of the human, altering microbial communities, and directly threatening human health and safety ([Shahid et al., 2021](#_bookmark111)). As a result, the development of effective techniques for the detection and removal of antibiotics is critical.

The Zhang, Y., et al. study focused on the application of AP-βCD-MOF

cross-linked with glutaraldehyde to improve the adsorption of tetracy-cline (TC) in wastewater treatment. The maximum adsorption capacity of AP-βCD-MOF for TC at pH 6 is 166.4 mg/g. Furthermore, the adsorption rate held steady at 71 % even after four cycles of reuse. The primary driving force for TC adsorption relies on the π-π electron-donor-acceptor (EDA) interaction. Indeed, the TC's hydrophobic phenyl ring facilitates its affinity for the adsorbent's hydrophobic structure, allowing it to aggregate at hydrophobic sites via π-π EDA interaction, demon-strating a high affinity at these locations ([Zhang et al., 2024](#_bookmark154)).

# Removal/adsorption mechanisms

In the treatment of hydrophilic organic and inorganic materials, these molecules are primarily adsorbed through chemical interactions or noncovalent bonds with the outer hydrophilic portion of the CD. The most commonly reported adsorption mechanisms include physical adsorption, chemical interaction, electrostatic adsorption, and adsorp-tion precipitation ([Tian et al., 2021](#_bookmark125)).

Remediation of heavy metals from water by MOFs occurs through physical and chemical adsorption, depending on the interaction be-tween adsorbents (MOFs) and adsorbates (heavy metals). Chemical adsorption, also known as reactive adsorption, contrasts with physical adsorption, which is referred to as adsorptive adsorption. The strength of physical and chemical adsorption considerably influences the adsorptive capacity of MOFs ([Rani et al., 2020](#_bookmark105)). The general mechanism for the removal of dye or heavy metals using cyclodextrin-based ad-sorbents is electrostatic interactions, complexation, or ion exchange ([Yadav et al., 2022](#_bookmark144)). Furthermore, the adsorbent containing multi-functional groups (e.g., N, O, S) can enhance heavy metal ion adsorption through coordination or electron donation ([Vo et al., 2020](#_bookmark129)).

In the study by Jia et al., it was mentioned that adsorption is domi-nated by single-layer chemisorption, as evidenced by adsorption kinetics and isotherm studies. This indicates the presence of hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction between carboxyl or hydroxyl groups on eco-friendly βCD-based nanocubes (βCD-MOF crosslinked with citric acid) and pollutants. In these adsorbents, the CDs' cavity also acts as an important key in the purifying of pollutants. Additionally, the host-guest interaction between CD-MOFs' cavity and dye molecules, as well as the chelation of heavy metal ions by –COOH functional groups also contribute significantly to the removal of the pollutants ([Jia et al.,](#_bookmark56) [2023](#_bookmark56)). The creation of stable inclusion compounds between the cavities of CDs and molecules can be utilized for sewage purification ([Tian et al.,](#_bookmark125) [2021](#_bookmark125)). At lower dosages of adsorbent, fewer adsorption sites are avail-able, leading to increased adsorption efficiency as the adsorbent dosage rises. However, the excess adsorbent dosages may result in competition for adsorption sites and kinetic energy consumption, which can ulti-mately reduce the overall adsorption efficiency ([Zhang, Zhang, Wang,](#_bookmark155) [et al., 2023](#_bookmark155)). Moreover, the zero-point charge (ZPC) of βCD-MOF at different pH values can act as a critical factor in the MOFs' adsorption capacity. When the pH of solution is below the pHzpc, the MOF surface bears a positive charge, while when the pH exceeds the pHZPC, the surface becomes negatively charged ([Kodama & Sekiguchi, 2006](#_bookmark69)). Consequently, a direct correlation exists between the ZPC and the adsorption efficiency: a higher ZPC favors the removal of anions, whereas a lower ZPC favors the removal of cations ([Zhang, Zhang,](#_bookmark155) [Wang, et al., 2023](#_bookmark155)).

Multiple mechanisms can be involved in the amide herbicides

adsorption by βCD-MOF-NPC, including π — π interaction, hydrogen bonding, and electrostatic interaction. The π — π interaction between the π-electrons in the carbon-based material and the π-rings of aromatic

adsorbates play a substantial role in the adsorption process. Further-more, two types of hydrogen bonds can be formed: dipole-dipole H-bonding occurs between hydroxyl groups (H-donors) on the surface of βCD-MOF-NPC and nitrogen or oxygen atoms (H-acceptors) of amide herbicides; whereas, Yoshida H-bonding forms between hydroxyl groups on the surface and aromatic rings of herbicides. Another mechanism

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Fig. 5.** Overview of beta-cyclodextrin-based metal-organic frameworks adsorption/removal mechanisms of pollutants.

involved is the electrostatic interaction owing to the effect of pH on both absorbents and absorbates ([Fig. 5](#_bookmark13)) ([Liu et al., 2019b](#_bookmark81)).

Generally, the operational pH and temperature play crucial roles in determining the efficiency of adsorption processes. It is essential to identify optimal conditions tailored to specific pollutant, as different metals exhibit varied adsorption behaviors under diverse conditions. Additionally, the initial concentration of heavy metals in wastewater directly impacts the design and capacity of the adsorption system. Sys-tems must be engineered to effectively manage fluctuating concentra-tions, ensuring high removal rates. Furthermore, optimizing the flow rate of wastewater through the adsorption system is vital to provide adequate contact time between the adsorbent and the heavy metals, thereby enhancing overall removal efficiency ([Qasem et al., 2021](#_bookmark100)).

# Challenges and future perspectives

The practical applications of βCD-MOF, particularly in pollutant removal, face several challenges and limitations. Understanding these issues is crucial for developing effective formulations and ensuring safety and efficacy. In terms of chemical and mechanical stability, it should be noted that CDs can be sensitive to environmental parameters such as pH, temperature, and humidity, which can compromise their effectiveness in pollutant removal applications. For example, βCD-MOFs may degrade in acidic environments due to competing protons coordi-nating with organic ligands, while basic conditions can lead to ligand replacement by hydroxide ions ([Lopez & Perez, 2023](#_bookmark85)).

The most important limitations are related to the ability of βCD-MOFs to maintain their structure under physical stress or deformation; therefore, βCD-MOFs have poor stability and binding specificity. Re-searchers are developing MOF-based membranes to enhance these properties by increasing surface area for better ligand binding, which is critical for practical applications in filtration and separation processes ([Njaramba et al., 2024](#_bookmark95)). Efforts are also underway to improve the cost-effectiveness and scalability of MOF synthesis for industrial use. The incorporation of βCD into MOF membranes has been shown to enhance mechanical properties. For example, membranes that combine βCD with

polymers exhibit improved mechanical strength and flexibility ([Wang,](#_bookmark131) [Huang, et al., 2023](#_bookmark131)).

While βCD derivatives like sulfobutyl ether β-cyclodextrin (SBE-βCD) and hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HP-βCD) are FDA-approved for specific applications, βCD itself lacks similar regulatory approval for parenteral use due to its nephrotoxic potential ([Stella & He, 2008](#_bookmark119)).

Compared to other MOFs, which may have varying degrees of biocompatibility and regulatory status, βCD-MOFs require careful consideration regarding their application in clinical settings and drug delivery. CD-MOFs are promising to adsorb various environmental contaminants, including heavy metals, pesticides, and organic solvents ([Sun et al., 2022](#_bookmark121); [Zhang, Zhang, Wang, et al., 2023](#_bookmark155)). Their high binding affinity for these pollutants allows effective removal from water sources, contributing to cleaner ecosystems. Comprehensive studies on their long-term environmental effects are still lacking. Understanding how these materials behave over time in natural ecosystems is essential to assessing their sustainability. The synthesis of βCD-MOFs can be com-plex and costly, particularly when involving specialized methods or reagents. This may limit their widespread adoption in industrial appli-cations or large-scale production.

# Conclusion

Beta-cyclodextrin-based metal-organic frameworks (βCD-MOFs) have emerged as a promising class of materials with significant potential in various applications, particularly in environmental remediation. This review has highlighted the versatility, biocompatibility, and effective-ness of βCD-MOFs in addressing critical environmental challenges. The synthesis methods for βCD-MOFs have evolved from traditional vapor diffusion to more advanced techniques such as hydro/solvothermal and ultrasound-assisted methods, allowing for greater control over crystal size, morphology, and functionality. Furthermore, the modification and functionalization of βCD-MOFs have expanded their capabilities, enhancing their stability in aqueous environments and improving their adsorption properties. βCD-MOFs have demonstrated remarkable effi-ciency in the removal of various pollutants from water, including heavy

metals, dyes, and nitroaromatic compounds, with adsorption capacities often surpassing those of conventional adsorbents. Their effectiveness can be attributed to their unique structural features, including high surface area, tunable pore size, and the presence of both hydrophilic and hydrophobic domains. The adsorption mechanisms of βCD-MOFs are diverse, involving electrostatic interactions, complexation, hydrogen bonding, and π-π interactions, making them versatile adsorbents capable of tackling a wide range of environmental contaminants. Despite these promising results, challenges remain, including the need for large-scale production methods and further investigation of long-term stability in diverse environmental conditions. Future research should focus on enhancing selectivity for specific pollutants, exploring potential in gas phase pollutant removal, investigating performance in complex envi-ronmental matrices, developing novel functionalization strategies, and assessing long-term environmental impact and safety. In conclusion, βCD-MOFs represent a significant advancement in environmental remediation, and as research progresses, they are likely to play an increasingly significant role in creating more sustainable and cleaner environments.
